# Google Antigravity (反重力) Community Full-Platform Chinese Deep Localization and Agent-Assist Pack

---

> ⚠️ **Important Notice and Disclaimer**
>
> 1. **Unofficial, self-initiated project**: This project is individually created and maintained by open-source community developers. It has no official affiliation, authorization, sponsorship, or endorsement from Google LLC, the Antigravity team, or VS Code.
> 2. **Purpose**: Because the official Antigravity client does not yet include a Chinese language pack option, this project aims to give Chinese-speaking developers an authentic, professional, and accessible development and agent-collaboration experience.
> 3. **Security commitment**: This project is fully open source. It does not collect, record, or upload any user code, tokens, or personal data, and all patch logic is transparent and visible.

## 📸 Localization Preview (Screenshots)

### 1. Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`) with Full Chinese Commands

### 2. Global General Settings and Agent Execution Permission Center

### 3. Full Set of 126 Official Skill Cards and Detailed Applicability Scenarios, Deeply Localized

---

## 💡 Notes on Antigravity 2.10.0+ Compatibility and Avoiding Pitfalls with Older Versions

Many developers who upgraded to Antigravity 2.10.0+ find that older Chinese patch packs from the internet no longer work, or even crash the program. Here are the core changes in 2.10.0+ and this project's targeted optimizations:

1. **Why do old patches get stuck on the Loading white screen in 2.10.0?**
   - In version 2.10.0, the official side refactored the lifecycle and destruction mechanism for window creation and the loading animation (`loadingOverlay.js`);
   - Early community patches (targeting 2.8.x / 2.9.x) mostly injected text by directly modifying the loading animation. In the new version this cuts off the official callback handshake, leaving the window stuck on the spinning screen;
   - This project **does not touch any official core files**. It uses an independent `preload.js` sandbox with delayed mounting. In testing, it opens instantly, with no spinning and no deadlock.

2. **Full support for the 110 official plugin skills added in 2.10.0 (125 skills in total)**:
   - 2.10.0 officially launched the Google Developer Plugins ecosystem;
   - Old patches covered only about a dozen early skills, which left much of the settings in English. This project fully covers all 125 skills, including BigQuery, Firebase, Flutter, Science, HyperFrames, and their detailed applicability descriptions.

3. **Alignment with the new version's changes**:
   - Deeply aligned with the redesigned 2.10.0 command palette (`Commands ⌵`), multi-device collaboration QR code scanning (`Remote Control`), and newly added theme presets such as `One Light` and `Solarized Light`.

Baskerville42/outage-data-ua.body:
# outage-data-ua

A public repository and tools for automatically collecting, parsing, visualizing (HTML), and automatically generating PNG images of scheduled and emergency power outage schedules in Ukraine.

The project retrieves data from open web pages of power suppliers and stores it as JSON "as is" in the `data/` directory. This data is then rendered in a fixed HTML template and converted into PNG images, which are saved to `images/<region>/gpv-x-x.png`.

---

## Data format
Each region is stored in a file `data/<region>.json`. Basic structure (abridged):

```json
{
  "regionId": "kyiv",
  "regionAffiliation": "м. Київ",
  "lastUpdated": "2025-11-06T11:41:56.430Z",
  "fact": { "updateFact": "06.11.2025 09:09" },
  "preset": { "updateFact": "04.11.2025 18:00" },
  "lastUpdateStatus": { "status": "parsed", "ok": true, "code": 200, "message": null, "at": "2025-11-06T11:41:56.430Z", "attempt": 5 },
  "meta": { "schemaVersion": "1.0.0", "contentHash": "..." }
}
```

- `preset` — scheduled outages for the week for each group (weekly template). Stored "as is", without structural normalization.
- `fact` — actual and emergency outages for today and tomorrow for each group. Also…

## 🌠 Wish-Based Generation: State Your Wish, Not the Steps

Making a set of game art assets used to mean: pick a model → tune parameters → connect nodes → cut out → split layers → edit text → export → redo……

In AI Art Engine, you only need to do one thing: **make a wish**.

> 🙏 "Give me a set of xianxia-style backpack UI, split into a PSD where the text can be edited directly, and also output Unity code."

Then the wish is fulfilled like this:

```
Your wish ─▶ Agent understands intent ─▶ automatically builds a workflow on the canvas ─▶ schedules models and local vision compute ─▶ delivers an editable project
```

When the wish comes true, you get **not an image, but a project that can go straight into your pipeline**:

| The wish you make | What you get |
| :--- | :--- |
| "Split this interface screenshot into layers at professional artist level" | Control-level layered `.psd` with double-click editable text + engine UI code |
| "Make this character portrait move" | Spine project package with skeleton and animations |
| "Turn this script into a one-minute short drama" | MP4 final cut + Jianying draft for further fine editing |

---

## 🧪 Wish Recipe: Reproduce the Entire Pipeline from One PNG (Workflow-in-PNG)

Every workflow that runs from a wish can be exported as a **recipe card (`.png`)** with the complete node graph embedded as lossless metadata (`tEXt(aiae:graph)`). Drag the original image back onto the software canvas to restore the full node topology, the 3D director's stage preview, and the prompt parameters in one click:

---

## ✨ Why Wishes Come True Here

**🧭 Wishes are not black boxes.**
Every wish is translated into a node workflow on the canvas that you can **see and modify**. If a step is unsatisfactory, open and change one node, or add another sentence. Only the changed parts are rerun. Wishes you have made are saved into the output PNG and can be fully reproduced by dragging it back onto the canvas.

**📦 Wishes become "projects," not "dead images."**
Our delivery standard: professional artists and programmers can pick it up and keep working. Layered, text-editable, stateful, and importable into engines, not a flat image that can only be regenerated.

**🔓 Make wishes to any model.**
30+ cloud models and local ComfyUI / Ollama can be switched freely. Bring your own key, local-first. Projects are ordinary folders on your disk. Built-in offline OCR and local vision models let many wishes come true even without a network connection.

LarryE135/dsh-flash-presets.body:
# dsh-flash-presets

DSH agent presets for the DeepSeek V4.1 Flash routing tier, delivered as a DSH bundle (`dsh.bundle`). After installation, several lines of `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` are inserted into the profile's plugin list. Host code is not modified, and the shared tool registry is not touched.

The presets affect three things: budget and turn count (counted per turn, not per step), folding and trimming of tool output, and the criteria for judging task completion. They do not improve model capability. They only determine how many turns a session uses, at which step it stops, and what standard it uses to wrap up.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Current version: v0.2.5 (GitHub Release and npm are both 0.2.5). The plan mode plugin `dsh-plan-mode-ui`, version 0.5.2, **ships together with the main version** (it is not released separately on Release, not tagged separately, and still not on npm). `v3` (internal codename lean-v3) is the main version, aligned with DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 and the v41flash 1017 snapshot.
> Verified: installer regression on three platforms; simulated installation (after installing with a temporary `DSH_HOME`, `dsh 0.2.1 --dump-config` synthesizes the three presets; repeated installation is idempotent; after uninstalling, no residue remains in dependencies, bundle selection, or patch layers); bundle composition consistency.
> Not verified: real macOS machine; same-scale comparison in native mode.
> For figures and failure scenarios, see [Measured Evidence](https://github.com/LarryE135/dsh-flash-presets/blob/HEAD/docs/实测证据.md) and the "Known Limitations" section below.

## Presets

| Preset | id | order | Number of rules | Compression | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| v1 | `flash-lean-ptc-v1` | 21 | 14 | 0.3 / 50k | Prioritizes context headroom, for longer tasks (comparison version, not installed by default) |
| v2 | `flash-lean-ptc-v2` | 22 | 12 | 0.25 / 20k | Same generation as v1, more economical, conservative choice (comparison version, not installed by default) |
| v3 | `flash-lean-ptc-v3` | 27 | 13 | 0.25 / 20k | **Installed by default**, the currently applicable version |

**Only v3 is installed by default**: the npm package and the installers no longer insert v1/v2 lines, so after installation the preset list has just one additional entry. For A/B comparison, explicitly install all three with `bash scripts/install.sh --all-presets` or `pwsh scripts/install.ps1 -AllPresets` (the v1/v2 source files are still shipped with the package). For specific adaptation details, see the release notes.

Free Apple ID signing typically expires after 7 days. When the app won't open after expiration, reconnect the iPhone and press `Cmd + R` in Xcode to reinstall and renew the signing for 7 more days:

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview
source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22
npx cap open ios
```

```bash
cd /Users/max/Desktop/github/interview

source ~/.nvm/nvm.sh && nvm use 22.22.2
```

MetalRiver/cabinet-drawer.body:
# Drawer (抽屉柜)

**A local-first Windows desktop “drawer”: store apps, files, URLs, snippets and passwords in one small window, ready to grab at any time.**

No account required · No reliance on cloud services · No telemetry · Data stays only on your computer

---

## What is this

Drawer (抽屉柜) is a desktop organizing tool for heavy Windows users. Frequently used applications, files, folders, and URLs, the commands and snippets you use every day, and your scattered passwords all go into one lightweight small window. Fit what you can, and search to find what you need. Lock your screen with one click when you step away, and password fields are stored encrypted.

## Why Drawer

- **Cluttered desktop, slow to find things**: frequently used entry points are scattered across the desktop, Start menu, and browser bookmarks. Drawer gathers them into one window with global search.
- **Lots of repetitive work**: the same command or text gets typed several times a day. Put it in the snippet library and copy it with one click.
- **Want to manage passwords yourself**: if you don't trust putting passwords in the cloud, Drawer's passwords are stored only in your local database.
- **Don't want to install five more tools**: launcher, snippet library, sticky notes, and password book in one app. No account registration, ready to use right after installing.

## Feature overview

| Module | Capability |
| :--- | :--- |
| 🗂️ **Apps** | Store applications / URLs / folders with automatic type detection. Can scan the Start menu and desktop, or drag in files for automatic categorization. Click to open. |
| ⭐ **Favorites** | Records usage count and last-used time. Frequently used items are aggregated for direct access. |
| 🔐 **Passwords** | Password fields are encrypted and stored locally. Viewing or copying a password requires re-verifying the master password. Supports title, username, URL, and notes. |
| 🗒️ **Snippets** | Save and copy common text, command lines, and code snippets with one click. |
| 📝 **Temporary** | Drafts and notes held temporarily, automatically cleared after 3 days (configurable). |
| 🗑️ **Recycle Bin** | Deleted content goes to the recycle bin first, where it can be restored or permanently deleted. |
| 🔒 **Lock** | Manual one-click lock. Auto-locks when idle (default 5 minutes, configurable). |
| 🟢 **Tray** | Runs in the background without taking up the taskbar. Quick actions via the tray icon. |

Pokanshuu/OC-Studio.body:
# OC Studio

A local-first workbench for original characters (OCs) and worldbuilding.

Current version: **v0.19.1-beta**

---

## Features

**Overview (home)**
Opening the app shows the world overview: world name and synopsis, counts of characters, events, countries, and entries, main characters, and recent updates. The "Home" entry at the top of the sidebar always returns you here.

**Characters / Events / Countries**
Full character info cards (synopsis, biography, portrait, birthday as year/month/day). Events support time spans and negative years. Countries can be linked to characters and events.

**Worldbuilding encyclopedia**
Tree-structured entry editor with `[[` internal links and `@` references for linking lore across entries. The hierarchy is the directory structure, so exporting the site turns it directly into chapters.

**Timeline**
Year, decade, fifty-year, and century aggregate views. Events are shown as rectangular bars and can be dragged to adjust timing. Character birthdays automatically become "X born" nodes. Period bars mark historical eras, with 6 selectable colors.

**Relationship graph**
A visual network of characters, events, and countries with 6 relationship types. Clicking a node jumps to its editor.

**Editor**
Slash commands, Markdown shortcut input, tables, to-do lists, and drag-to-reorder blocks. All modules share the same core.

**Global album**
Image fields from characters, events, and countries are aggregated automatically, with a two-level category tree and search filtering.

**Dark mode**
Light / night / follow system, with full design-token coverage.

**Global search**
`Ctrl+K` for fuzzy search across modules, `Ctrl+S` to save.

**Recycle bin**
Soft delete with restore and permanent delete. Items are cleaned up automatically after 30 days.

**Data import/export**
`.ocbak` JSON format with 4 merge strategies (skip / overwrite / keep both / clear and import).

**Static showcase site export**
Export an entire world with one click into a single `index.html`, with content, styles, scripts, and images all inlined. Rename it to `index.html` and publish to GitHub Pages or any static host, or open it offline.

**Repository: folder-based lore collection (desktop)**
Store a lore collection as an ordinary folder. Entries are Markdown with frontmatter, so you can open them directly in Obsidian and version them with Git. Changes are written back to the files in real time, and **unedited notes are left completely untouched**. To move to another machine, just copy the folder.

---

## Planned

- Custom collections (lightweight database): collections, records, custom fields, relations, and reverse "belongs to" links.
- Image export templates, relationship graph rewrite, album / image component atomization, web export templates.
- Theme system, community templates, and plugins (long term).

For schedule and requirements, see `docs/todo.md` and `docs/自定义分类-需求文档.md`.

TaoistLuo/OmniBinder.body:
# OmniBinder

Chinese | [English](https://github.com/TaoistLuo/OmniBinder/blob/HEAD/README.en.md)

**A cross-platform service communication middleware for embedded and distributed service scenarios**

OmniBinder is a cross-platform service communication middleware for embedded systems, desktops, distributed multi-board systems, and multi-service collaboration scenarios. It currently supports **Linux** and **Windows**, with plans for Android, HarmonyOS, FreeRTOS/ESP32, and others. In principle, any platform that supports TCP sockets and a C++11 compiler can be ported. Only about 20 platform abstraction functions need to be implemented. See the [platform porting guide](https://github.com/TaoistLuo/OmniBinder/blob/HEAD/docs/platform-porting.md).
Its goal is not only to solve “how processes pass data,” but to solve **how multiple services register, get discovered, are invoked, broadcast, and become state-aware in a unified way**.
By providing a unified entry point for service communication and management, along with automatically selected SHM/TCP data channels, OmniBinder lets cross-process, cross-board, and cross-device service collaboration be integrated under one consistent model.

In one sentence: **OmniBinder is middleware that acts as a communication bridge between distributed services, standardizing how services connect, invoke each other, and distribute data.**

---

## Project Background

In embedded, industrial, and edge computing scenarios, a complete system is usually not a single monolithic program. Instead, multiple services work together: sensor acquisition, algorithm processing, device control, gateway forwarding, HMI display, logging and monitoring, and other modules often run in different processes, on different boards, or even on different devices.

The hard part is often not “a single socket send,” but **how to stably connect these scattered services into a communication bridge that can be discovered, invoked, broadcast to, and state-aware**:

- How services are discovered by other modules after they start
- How services are invoked in a unified way, instead of each module writing its own communication protocol
- How state and events are broadcast to multiple consumers
- How other modules can perceive and recover when a service exits unexpectedly
- How the business layer can keep its interfaces unchanged when deployment changes between same-machine and cross-machine setups

## Positioning Compared with Common Solutions

OmniBinder is not meant to replace all existing communication frameworks. It targets a more specific class of engineering problems: **when a system is made up of multiple services that may be distributed across the same machine, multiple boards, or multiple devices, how to use one unified model for service management and inter-service communication.**

From this perspective, common solutions can be understood as follows:

| Solution category | Representative solutions | Better-suited scenarios | Difference from OmniBinder |
|---|---|---|---|
| Local IPC / service bus | Android Binder, D-Bus | Same-machine service-oriented communication, system service orchestration, local process collaboration | …

# Dddify Admin

Dddify Admin is a modern admin system template based on **ASP.NET Core + React**. # @dsh-external/dsh-ui-progress

DSH Web UI session progress plugin: provides a persistent session progress bar in the input dock area of the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI, **zero core changes** (pure client plugin, does not touch agent-loop).

> **Your DSH version determines which plugin version to install** (installing the wrong one will crash; common symptom: `useConversation is not a function`)
>
> - DSH **0.1.2-alpha.1 ~ 0.2.1-alpha.1**: install the **new version** (default command below; for the plugin tag corresponding to each DSH version, see the [version compatibility table](#版本对应--version-compatibility))
> - Older DSH (0.1.1-rc.2 and earlier): **no available version**
>

## Installation

> **Installation method (auto-mounted since v0.11.4)**: Since v0.11.4, this package ships with `cordis.patch.yml` and declares `dsh.bundle.patch`. After `dsh plugin --profile web add` installation, it **automatically registers the profile layer and mounts**, so you no longer need to hand-write `insert` config lines (deployments pinned to older tags still need them). **GUI note**: the plugin page's "Add plugin" only accepts registry package names or local directory paths. `name@github:owner/repo#tag` is a pnpm alias spec (CLI only); pasting it into the GUI raises `ERR_PNPM_INVALID_PACKAGE_NAME`. In the GUI, clone the repo and use the local directory path, or wait for npm publication and use the package name.

```sh
# Option 1: git dependency pinned to a tag (public mirror, recommended; github:lhh010/dsh-ui-progress also works)
dsh plugin --profile web add '@dsh-external/dsh-ui-progress@github:lhh010/dsh-ui-progress#v0.11.9'

# Option 2: local link (development)
git clone https://github.com/lhh010/dsh-ui-progress.git
cd dsh-ui-progress && pnpm install && pnpm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-ui-progress
```

soulmachine/ubuntu-provision.body:
# Ubuntu Provision

Uses Ansible to automate **Ubuntu** development environment setup: system software is installed via **apt**, language runtimes are handled by mise, and other tools follow each tool's official `curl | sh` install scripts and `npm` / `bun` / `uv` global packages. The shell is Ubuntu's built-in **bash**, configured with starship, zoxide, fzf, and Omarchy's shell environment.

This repository is the Ubuntu port of the sibling `macbook-provision` (macOS version), targeting **Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (amd64)**, serving the supermicro and grok-bot machines. The correspondence with upstream (synced commit, intentionally omitted roles) is recorded in the "Upstream" section of `AGENTS.md`, and every intentional difference is recorded in `DECISIONS.md`.

## Language Runtimes

This project uses [mise](https://github.com/jdx/mise) to install language runtimes (Go, Node.js, JDK, etc.) rather than the system package manager. mise is a multi-language version manager that supports installing and switching between multiple versions on the same machine, for example, freely switching between JDK 22 and JDK 23. mise is cross-platform, so this part is fully consistent with the macOS version. Python is the exception: it is managed by uv (`bootstrap.sh` installs 3.14 and does not overwrite the system `python3`).

## Usage

### 1. Install Ansible

```bash
./bootstrap.sh
```

This script configures passwordless sudo, installs apt base dependencies (`build-essential`, `curl`, `git`, `python3` / `python3-apt`, etc.), uv and Python 3.14, mise, and finally installs Ansible with `uv tool install --with ansible ansible-core`. It also adds `~/.local/bin` and mise's shims directory to the **top of `~/.bashrc`, above the non-interactive guard** (before `case $- in`), so that non-interactive shells such as `ssh host 'cmd'` can also find them.

> **About passwordless sudo**: Ansible tasks marked `become: true` (apt installs, apt repository setup for gh / Docker / Tailscale, etc.) need `sudo` not to prompt for a password when unattended. The script writes a rule to `/etc/sudoers.d/<username>-nopasswd` of the form `<username> ALL=(ALL)…`

# DataY · Lightweight Data Platform

> A data platform can be small without sacrificing features. With DataY running, you get data integration, dimensional modeling, task scheduling, a high-performance data warehouse, and intelligent data Q&A, all in one.

🌐 **Product homepage**: [http://datay.yuyuejia.com.cn/](http://datay.yuyuejia.com.cn/)

## Why DataY?

Traditional data platforms often require a dozen or more machines and hundreds of GB of memory, with complex deployment and high operating costs. DataY's philosophy is: **use a highly refined technology stack to slim things down, and deliver the most complete data capabilities.**

| Traditional approach | DataY |
|---|---|
| Requires multiple system components such as Hadoop / Spark / distributed schedulers | One JAR, in-house engine, all-in-one deployment, no component hell |
| Requires multiple servers to start | **2 cores, 4 GB** is enough to run the full pipeline from data integration → data warehouse → data Q&A |
| Complex tech stack and high operations barrier, requires dedicated big data engineers | Zero-dependency startup, development environment set up in 10 minutes |

**DataY = DataX + Nifi + DolphinScheduler**, but it is not a patchwork of three tools. Instead, these three categories of capability have been redesigned as a single runtime:

- A self-developed unified stream-batch data integration framework, responsible for 'getting data in and computing it efficiently';
- A self-developed distributed scheduling framework, responsible for 'scheduling accurately and running stably';
- AI-native capabilities, responsible for 'being usable and automatable.'

Here, 'lightweight' refers to **a low barrier to runtime resources**, not to lightweight capabilities. It does not depend on heavy components such as Hadoop or Spark. A single JAR is enough to start it. It supports DuckDB as a high-performance analytics engine, as well as analytics engines such as Doris and CLickHouse. A development machine with 2 cores and 4 GB can run the full pipeline from data ingestion to report querying.

## Project Structure

DataY has two submodules: Core provides the engine, and Web provides the platform product:

```
datay/
├── pom.xml          # Maven parent module
├── datay-core/      # Lightweight, high-performance, unified stream-batch data integration engine
├── datay-web/       # Visual data platform (task design + scheduling + data warehouse + data Q&A)
└── docs/            # Product homepage + help documentation
```

## Quick Start

Download the command-line program for your platform from [Release](https://github.com/zc310/ofd/releases) and run it. In file names, `darwin` means macOS and `amd64` applies to 64-bit Intel/AMD computers. For the full mapping table, see the [Release package download guide](https://github.com/zc310/ofd/blob/HEAD/docs/RELEASE-ASSETS.md):

```bash
# OFD to PDF
ofd-converter input.ofd output.pdf
```
